solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Indian dish served in Maryland port? No more

indicators.note: read literally, the words tell you to remove those very letters from the place name

blocks.note: the largest port city in the US state of Maryland
the word itself, the part taken away

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether a curry can still be had in an American harbour city, only to be told it has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No more' sounds like the kitchen has sold out; in fact it says strip MORE from BALTIMORE, leaving BALTI.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spicy curry cooked and served in a metal bowl, popularised in Birmingham's South Asian restaurants.

clue.text: A Jurassic herbivore, or a son 18 abandoned?

indicators.note: to act abandoned is to behave wildly and without restraint, so the letters run riot into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the answer to 18 across

explanation.surface: It asks whether a giant plant-eater might be a child that Brutus left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: A cross-reference: 18 is the answer to 18 across, BRUTUS, whose letters join OR A SON for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The brontosaurus was a huge long-necked sauropod dinosaur living in the late Jurassic period and eating vegetation.

clue.text: Nonsense writer engaging husband as composer of music

indicators.note: to engage someone is to take them on, so one piece takes another into itself

blocks.note: Edward Lear, Victorian author of nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A writer of comic verse hires a married man to write the score.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Lehar wrote operettas, most famously The Merry Widow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lehar was an Austro-Hungarian composer best remembered for light operettas, so he is a writer of music.

clue.text: Mongoose in Germany I associated with cardinal in speech

indicators.note: something in speech is spoken rather than written, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: ICH is the German word for I
John Henry Newman, the Victorian cardinal, now a saint

explanation.surface: A German speaker introduces themself alongside a churchman while talking about a small mammal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' could be a number or a bird; here it is Cardinal Newman, whose name is said to give the ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichneumon is the old name for the Egyptian mongoose, a small carnivore revered in ancient Egypt for killing snakes.

clue.text: Bog standard wine about to overcome character opening inn

indicators.note: an opening is a beginning, so only the first letter of the word is wanted
to overcome is to come over the top of, so the earlier pieces straddle another

blocks.note: a red Bordeaux wine from the Medoc region
RE is Latin for concerning, used as about
surface padding: it only says that what follows is a single letter
the letter at the head of the word

explanation.surface: An ordinary house wine is served on arrival at a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' does double duty in the eye but only one job: it gives RE, while 'to overcome' tells the wine to sit astride the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bog standard is British slang for plain, ordinary and unremarkable, which is what mediocre quality amounts to.

clue.text: Flowering plant requiring market’s first permit

indicators.note: first points to the leading letter only, discarding the rest of the word

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
to permit is to let something happen

explanation.surface: A flower seller needs a licence before setting up a stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Permit' reads as a noun in the surface but works as the verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallows are a family of plants with pink or purple blooms, including the hollyhock and marsh species.

clue.text: Doctor once said to be connected with Bath and Wells perhaps

definitions.text: connected with Bath and Wells perhaps

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A former physician was rumoured to have links with a pair of English spa towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person; it is a verb meaning tamper with. Bath and Wells is a Church of England diocese in Somerset, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Diocesan means belonging to a diocese, the district a bishop oversees, and Bath and Wells is one such Anglican district.

clue.text: Eg Hammerstein’s gigantic vehicle?

blocks.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a car is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: It asks whether a famous lyricist drove a huge car.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive hides the definition: Hammerstein's first name. 'Eg' signals that it is one example of a person bearing that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Hammerstein II was the Broadway lyricist partnered with Richard Rodgers, so his given name was Oscar.

clue.text: Sorry about worker shut up inside

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the walls of the others

blocks.note: RE is Latin for concerning, used as about
pent, as in pent-up, means confined
the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: An employee feels bad after being locked indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' looks like an order to be quiet; it means confined, as in pent-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sorry for their wrongdoing feels remorse, which is exactly the state of a penitent person.

clue.text: Work with the school map, perhaps: it’s for examining pupils

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words may come out some other way, so their letters are rearranged

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work
taken as written

explanation.surface: A geography lesson in which a teacher uses a wall chart to test the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupils' suggests schoolchildren, chiming with the school map, but these are the pupils of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An ophthalmoscope is the optician's lit instrument for looking through the eye's dark opening at the retina behind it.

clue.text: Representative of Evita touring south pursuing wheel components?

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it, so one piece encircles another
to pursue is to follow behind, so this part comes after the other

blocks.note: the rods running from hub to rim
Eva Peron, Argentina's first lady, known as Evita
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: An envoy for Argentina's famous first lady travels south behind a set of bicycle parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Evita is the nickname of Eva Peron, so her surname is wanted; it goes round S and follows the wheel parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokesperson speaks on behalf of an organisation or group, acting as its official voice and delegate.

clue.text: Small group Elder perhaps notes outside hotel

indicators.note: outside puts the earlier piece around the next one

blocks.note: the elder is a kind of tree, with perhaps marking an example
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
SO and ME, two notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A few church elders make music outside a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elder' suggests a senior person, but it is the shrub; TREE goes round H, and the notes SO and ME follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A threesome is a set of three people, which is about as small as a gathering can get after a pair.

clue.text: Athlete’s approach getting old rail union down?

blocks.note: surface reading: a defunct railway union going under
setter's reading: treat the answer as an instruction, a word followed by a direction, and it spells the National Union of Railwaymen, NUR, backwards

explanation.surface: A sprinter's approach seems tied to the collapse of a former railway trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as RUN going UP, and the letters reverse to NUR, the old National Union of Railwaymen, now merged away, hence old and down.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up is the stretch of running a jumper, bowler or thrower makes before the leap, delivery or throw.

clue.text: Obsequious sergeant major and his area of influence

blocks.note: SM is the abbreviation for sergeant major
a sergeant major holds sway in the army

explanation.surface: A fawning senior soldier and the force where he wields power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' refers back to the sergeant major, whose domain is the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy describes oily, ingratiating behaviour, the insincere flattery of someone sucking up to superiors.

clue.text: Old Native American, key one of five inspiring long novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form
to inspire is to breathe in, so the pair draws another piece inside

blocks.note: A is a musical key
taken as written
a quin is one of quintuplets

explanation.surface: An elderly Native American has a key role in a long novel about quintuplets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' sounds like a book, but it is the adjective meaning new. A is the musical key, and a quin is one of quintuplets.
explanation.definitionFit: The Algonquin are a First Nations people of the Ottawa valley region, so a member is an indigenous North American.

clue.text: Eye-catching feature high-flyer goes round with minder at first

indicators.note: at first means at the beginning, so only the leading letter is wanted
to go round something is to encircle it

blocks.note: the skylark sings as it climbs high
with and and both join things together
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An ambitious executive tours a striking sight with a bodyguard in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flyer' suggests a successful person; here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A landmark is a prominent building or natural object that stands out and helps people find their way.

clue.text: Dreadful pranks reportedly stopped by cold woman in charge

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound counts rather than the spelling
a stopper plugs a gap, so a letter is wedged into the middle

blocks.note: dire means dreadful
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
pranks are tricks

explanation.surface: A frosty female boss puts an end to some awful practical jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: The C plugs the gap between the two halves of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Directrix is the old feminine form of director, so it names a female person who directs or manages things.

clue.text: Likable prayers introducing a set of holy books

indicators.note: to introduce is to come before and present what follows

blocks.note: pleas are earnest requests, as prayers are
taken as written
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: Agreeable prayers serve as a preface to scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Testament is a collection of books, hence set.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone or something agreeable and nice to be around, giving enjoyment and goodwill.

clue.text: Old city bloke left Derby finally as a top priority

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter only

blocks.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
gent is a man
L is the abbreviation for left
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man quits the English city of Derby as a matter of urgency.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, in modern Iraq, is the crossword's favourite ancient city. Derby is a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something as a top priority means doing it before anything else, pressingly and without delay.

clue.text: Dry American senator in Rome way back

blocks.note: brut describes very dry champagne
US for American

explanation.surface: A teetotal American politician sits in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Senator' pulls towards Washington, but the senator is in ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Junius Brutus was a member of the ancient Roman senate and a leading assassin of Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Comedian’s foil swapping a ring for daughter’s heavy food

indicators.note: to swap is to exchange one thing for another

blocks.note: a stooge is the straight man who sets up a comic's jokes
a ring is round like the letter O
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A comic's sidekick trades a wedding band for his daughter's filling meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The second O of STOOGE is replaced by D. Stodge is British slang for heavy, starchy food such as suet pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is filling, starchy, rather indigestible fare of the dumpling and steamed pudding sort.

clue.text: “Like a bone?” First of underfed Labradors raced back

definitions.note: adjective: of the ulna, a forearm bone

indicators.note: first of points to the leading letter of each word that follows
going back means running in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the opening letter
the opening letter
ran is the past tense of run, meaning raced

explanation.surface: Hungry dogs dash back asking whether there is a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of' covers both underfed and Labradors. The question mark warns that 'Like a bone' is a cryptic way of saying relating to one particular bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulnar means relating to the ulna, the inner of the two long bones of the human forearm.

clue.text: Libertines encountered in Marrakesh?

indicators.note: something encountered in a place is met there, sitting inside it

blocks.note: letters three to seven of the city name

explanation.surface: Debauched pleasure-seekers turn up in a Moroccan city.
explanation.walkthrough: Marrakesh is a city in Morocco.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute, pleasure-seeking man of loose morals, just as a libertine is.

clue.text: Lorry governor used to carry agreed plant

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within

blocks.note: artic is British shorthand for an articulated lorry
HE, His Excellency, is a governor's title
OK means agreed

explanation.surface: A truck once belonging to a governor is used to transport an approved vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: A lorry is the British word for a truck, and an artic is one with a separate cab and trailer. His Excellency is the formal title of a colonial governor.
explanation.definitionFit: The artichoke is a thistle-like plant whose edible flower buds, or else tubers in the Jerusalem kind, are eaten as vegetables.

clue.text: Old man carrying article made of wood

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
A is the indefinite article
Ken is a man's name

explanation.surface: An elderly man is carrying a wooden object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' looks like one unit meaning father; it splits into O and a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaken is an adjective for things fashioned from oak timber, one particular kind of wood.

clue.text: Game birds?

blocks.note: first meaning: the pastime of skimming flat stones across water
second meaning: female and male waterfowl

explanation.walkthrough: 'Game birds' reads as birds shot for sport; split it into a pastime and a pair of birds. Ducks and drakes is the British name for skimming stones.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a stone-skipping pastime and also literally lists female and male mallards together.

clue.text: A new compiler mostly imbibing single liqueur

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter
to imbibe is to drink in, so the earlier pieces take another inside

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
I is the Roman numeral one
a crossword compiler is called a setter

explanation.surface: A newly arrived crossword maker has a drink of liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: SETTER loses its last letter; A, N and SETTE together take in I.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured spirit of the liqueur sort, drunk diluted or neat after meals.

clue.text: Gaseous element unknown in French — or Norwegian originally

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so each word gives its first letter

blocks.note: X is the classic algebraic unknown
en is French for in
the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A mystery gas is named in French or in Norwegian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like a link, but its first letter is needed alongside Norwegian's.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is a colourless noble gas, chemical element number 54, used in bright lamps.
